{"slug": "build-a-agency-website-with-ai", "title": "How to Build an Agency Website with AI (No Code Needed)", "metaTitle": "How to Build an Agency Website with AI | Kodely", "metaDescription": "Learn how to build a full agency website with AI in minutes: services, portfolio, team, and contact sections, published free to a live URL with Kodely.", "targetKeyword": "build a agency website with AI", "category": "Use-Cases", "bodyHtml": "

What a good agency website actually needs

Before you write a single prompt, it helps to know what you are actually building. Most agency sites that convert visitors into leads share the same five ingredients, regardless of industry:

  • A clear value proposition — one sentence, above the fold, that says what you do and who it is for.
  • Services offered — a scannable breakdown of what a client can hire you to do.
  • Portfolio or case studies — proof that you have done this before and it worked.
  • Team — faces and names build trust faster than any tagline.
  • Contact — a low-friction way to start a conversation, whether that is a form, an email link, or both.

Everything else — testimonials, a blog, an FAQ section — is a bonus layered on top of those five. If you are just getting your agency site off the ground, get these right first.

The one-prompt approach

The traditional way to get this built is to hire a designer, brief a developer, wait two to six weeks, and pay a few thousand dollars for something you will want to tweak the moment it launches. The AI approach collapses that into a conversation. You describe the site you want in plain English, in as much or as little detail as you have, and the AI builds a working version immediately. You are not filling out a template or picking from a theme gallery — you are describing your agency, and getting a site built around that description.

The trick to getting a good first draft is being specific about the five ingredients above. A vague prompt like build me an agency website produces a generic result. A prompt that names your services, describes your visual style, and says how many case studies or team members to include produces something you can actually launch from.

A real example prompt

Here is a prompt that produces a solid first pass for a marketing agency:

Build a marketing agency website called Northlane Digital. Hero section with a bold headline about performance-driven marketing and a subheadline mentioning SEO, paid media, and content strategy. Below that, a services section with three cards: SEO, Paid Media, and Content Strategy, each with a short description. Add a portfolio section with six case study cards showing a client name, a one-line result, and a placeholder metric. Add a team section with four profile cards. Close with a contact section that has a name, email, and message form. Use a dark navy background with electric blue accents and a modern sans-serif look throughout.

Notice what that prompt does: it names the sections in order, gives the AI concrete counts (three services, six case studies, four team members), and specifies a color direction instead of leaving it to guesswork.

What Kodely actually generates

When you run a prompt like that in Kodely, you are not getting a static mockup or a page of raw HTML. Kodely generates a real Vite and React 19 application written in TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS v4, built from a foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives already in place. Each section of your site — the hero, the services grid, the portfolio cards, the contact form — is its own component file. The live preview you see while it builds is the actual compiled app running, not a static render standing in for one.

You can open the code view at any point and read or copy the exact source files being generated. There is no zip export or project download yet — code view is for reading and copying, not downloading a full project — but nothing is hidden from you.

Customizing via chat

Once the first draft is up, refine it the same way you built it: describe the change in chat. Swap the color scheme, add a fourth service, rewrite the hero headline, reorder the portfolio cards, or ask for a new section entirely. Kodely edits the real component files behind the scenes rather than regenerating the whole app, so changes are targeted.

If a change takes the site somewhere you did not want, every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint. Rolling back to an earlier version is free, so there is no risk in experimenting with a bolder layout or a different tone.

Publishing to a live URL

When the site looks right, one click publishes it to a real, public URL at yourname.kodely.site. There is no separate hosting step, no server to configure, and no extra cost — publishing is included. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so a stray key pasted into a prompt will not end up shipped to the public internet.

Credits and pricing

Kodely is metered on real AI cost through a credit system. New accounts get 750 credits free, no credit card required, which is enough to build and iterate on a full agency site. If a generation fails to compile, you are not charged for it. When you need more, top-ups are straightforward and credits never expire:

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe the site in chat and Kodely writes the actual React components. If you do know code, you can open code view and read exactly what was generated.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet. Every site published with Kodely today lives on a free yourname.kodely.site subdomain.

Can I download the project files?

Not currently. You can view and copy source files from the in-app code view, but there is no zip export or full project download yet.

Will the site include a contact form that actually sends email, or a database?

Kodely builds the front-end: layout, sections, styling, and content, including a contact form UI. It does not generate backend logic, databases, or authentication — for a typical agency marketing site, none of that is required to launch.

What if I do not like the first result?

Describe what to change in chat. If a change goes the wrong direction, roll back to any earlier checkpoint for free.
